doc.title: Documentation
doc.description: Generate the complete documentation for compliance

methodology.intro: This chapter documents the method the TARA was computed with. It is generated from the project configuration and from the rules the calculation applies, so it cannot describe another method than the one used.
methodology.scaleNotConforming: does not conform: ISO/SAE 21434 requires four impact ratings (RQ-15-05)

aggregation.harm-floor: harm to people / environment as floor, otherwise weighted mean
aggregation.weighted-mean: weighted mean of the rated factors

likelihoodMethod.iso-21434: attack feasibility (attack potential, Annex G.2 / ISO/IEC 18045)

likelihoodModel.feasibility-x-motivation: likelihood = feasibility combined with attacker benefit

methodology.bands: Attack feasibility from attack potential (Table G.7)
methodology.gateRulesIntro: How the children of an AND / OR node combine, per kind of leaf rating. The attack tree's feasibility is the most feasible path (15.8 NOTE 2).
methodology.treatmentIntro: The options are stored with TARAflow's values; the report shows the ISO names. A stored "transfer" is shown as "Share (transfer)" and flagged for review.
methodology.stampsIntro: Values computed now carry these stamps. A risk or attack-tree analysis with another stamp was computed with another version or other tables.
methodology.propertiesIntro: Every damage and threat scenario names the compromised property out of these seven. ISO/SAE 21434 (3.1.20) names confidentiality, integrity and availability as examples of cybersecurity properties; the further four are used as properties of their own.

propertyDef.C: Information is disclosed only to those entitled to it.
propertyDef.I: Data, code and functions are not altered without authorization.
propertyDef.A: The asset is usable when needed.
propertyDef.N: An action cannot later be denied by whoever performed it.
propertyDef.AuthN: The identity of a communication partner, user or message source is proven.
propertyDef.AuthZ: Only permitted subjects can perform an action or reach a resource.
propertyDef.Acc: Actions can be traced back to whoever performed them.

methodology.safetyLevelText: from the categorical severity: none → negligible, reversible → moderate, irreversible → major, fatal → severe. A safety rating given as a number is the Se factor: 1 and 2 → moderate, 3 → major, 4 → severe (4 stands for irreversible major or fatal) — unlike the other categories, 1 is not negligible here.
methodology.riskMatrix: Risk value (15.8): matrix of Annex H.8
methodology.riskMatrixIntro: The risk value 1–5 of a threat scenario (RQ-15-16) is read from this matrix: impact of the damage scenario (highest rated category) × attack feasibility. It is the informative example of ISO/SAE 21434 Annex H, Table H.8, used unchanged.

imported.groupSummary: {{count}} threat(s) of the component, each shown once for all its instances

cause.aou_evidence_pending: {{ref}} fulfilled by a measure not implemented yet

goalsClaims.intro: The outcome of the risk treatment decisions (ISO/SAE 21434 9.4, 15.9): a cybersecurity goal for every risk that is reduced, a cybersecurity claim for every risk that is retained or shared, and the verification of the TARA, the goals and the claims.

itemDefinition.intro: What the analysis is about (ISO/SAE 21434 9.3): the item's purpose and functions, its boundary, its preliminary architecture and its operational environment, with the sources they come from and the assumptions the analysis relies on.

neutral.intro: What the analysis is about: the system's intended purpose and functions, its boundary, its architecture and its operational environment, with the sources they come from and the assumptions the analysis relies on.

attackTrees.intro: One section per attack tree: its anchor, the tree structure with the AND/OR gates and the leaf ratings, and the attack paths derived from it with attack potential, attack feasibility and the analyst's relevance decision.
attackTrees.importedRatingText: Paths rated with this TARA's feasibility configuration; the window of opportunity of each step is this TARA's decision, per instance; the other factors are the component's.

compliance.intro: The requirements of IEC 62443-4-2 for the component, each with whether it applies and how it is met — the Statement of Applicability, derived from the analysed model. A row is met by the model, by a mitigation of the risk treatment, by a supporting measure outside the component, by an analyst statement or covered by a claim; the source is named for every row.
compliance.claimsText: Requirements the system around the component meets (supporting measure, CCSC 2; compensating countermeasure): they count for the value with measures of the system, not for the product itself. The integrator or operator confirms them.
compliance.introSrsl: The requirements of EN 50742 Approach A for the machine, each with whether it applies and how it is met, derived from the analysed model, the risks with their SRSL and the project data. A row is met by the model, by the mandated controls of the risk treatment or by an analyst statement; the source is named for every row.
compliance.introMixed: The requirements of each active standard, each with whether it applies and how it is met — derived from the analysed model, the risk treatment and the analyst statements; the source is named for every row. One part per standard.
compliance.srslText: The highest SRSL the rated risks give for each safety function (an asset with a physical impact), and the interfaces on a path to it — found backwards along the data flows from the safety function's elements. The SRSL is derived in the risk assessment; it is not entered here.
compliance.openText: Rows not yet met — each is closed by rating the risk, choosing and implementing the mandated control, completing the project data, or a statement with its evidence.
compliance.contradiction: mitigation marked done, but the model shows the requirement not met
compliance.modelChanged: the model changed since the statement — review it
compliance.superseded: statement kept from another device category — the row no longer applies
compliance.draft: draft, may change before it is cited
compliance.basisText: Requirements met only with the help of the system around the component are marked as {{ccsc2}} (CCSC 2); they appear in the second value of each foundational requirement.
compliance.vectorText: SL-T: what the operator or the zone requires. SL-C (product): what the product provides according to the model and the mitigations marked done; planned: after the chosen open mitigations. With measures of the system: what the plant can reach if it provides the listed supporting measures and claims — the basis for the SL-A, which only arises in the operated plant. ✗ marks a value below the SL-T.
compliance.craText: The essential cybersecurity requirements with the rows of the matrix behind them (EN IEC 62443-4-2/prAA, Annex ZZ). Part I (1), (2)(a) and (2)(g) and Part II are met by the development and vulnerability handling process (EN IEC 62443-4-1) — outside this matrix.
compliance.craDocumentation: Not part of this assessment: the information the CRA requires for the user and in the technical documentation (Annex II), such as the support period, the contact for reporting vulnerabilities and the product identification — it is stated in the product documentation.
compliance.gapsText: Rows needed for the SL-T that the product does not meet itself (SL-C) — each is closed by a change of the product (mitigation), a statement, or a measure the plant provides (supporting measure, claim).

uncountedClaims.unclear: claims unclear (assumption of use without evidence)
uncountedClaims.not_effective: claims not effective here (assumption of use not fulfilled)
uncountedClaims.partial: claims covering only part of the row's elements
